request.spec:
A grade merge is now retroactive: for every person it moves, every grade record of theirs on the
merged grade becomes the other grade, so all their claims, whatever their date, use the other
grade's rates (and its terms and thresholds) from then on. Frozen figures and figures bound by a
statement are unchanged.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A grade merge is now retroactive: for every person it moves, every grade record of theirs on the
merged grade becomes the other grade, so all their claims, whatever their date, use the other
grade's rates (and its terms and thresholds) from then on. Frozen figures and figures bound by a
statement are unchanged.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A grade merge is now retroactive, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. I only changed a comment in the front end after that run and didn't re-run it.

**What changed:**
- **`grade/MergeGrade.java`**: Each person is still moved and logged one at a time, exactly as before. After that loop, every grade record of theirs on the merged grade becomes the other grade, whatever its from-date. The rollup is then recalculated, so the closing whole-merge `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS` audit lines show the retroactive figures, in the order the test expects. Frozen figures and figures bound by a statement still come out unchanged, because the existing rollup already keeps them as they were.
- **`person/PersonRepository.java`**: a new `regrade(...)` method rewrites each matching grade record through the existing `saveGrade`.
- I also updated the comments describing the merge in `grade-merge.POST.yml` and `features/grades/api.ts`.

**One choice to check:** each rewritten record also gets a new history entry dated the sheet's today. So looking at the sheet as of a date before the merge still shows the old grades, and from the merge date on it shows the merged ones. The request didn't say how history should behave; tell me if you'd rather the old history be rewritten too.
